newsitem.title: USA: Pepsi appoints former president to head spin-off.
newsitem.headline: Pepsi appoints former president to head spin-off.

text.p: PepsiCo Inc. said Monday it will bring in Andrall Pearson, a former president of the corporation and now a top buyout firm executive, to head its $10 billion restaurant spin-off.
Pearson, an operating partner of Clayton, Dubilier & Rice, will become chairman of the new company, which has yet to be named.

The new company, with estimated revenues of $10 billion, will combine the worldwide businesses of Pizza Hut, Kentucky Fried Chicken and Taco Bell. It will be the world's largest restaurant company in units and second-largest in sales, with more than 29,000 restaurants in 95 countries, PepsiCo said.
A former Harvard Business School professor with experience in the consumer products, retailing and franchising industries, Pearson will set the overall strategy for the new company.

For a large part of his career, Pearson was president and chief operating officer of PepsiCo and was involved in acquiring and expanding Pizza Hut and Taco Bell. Pearson earlier spent 16 years at McKinsey & Co., where he was a director and led the firm's marketing practice.
PepsiCo said David Novak, president and chief executive of Pizza Hut and KFC, will serve as the new company's vice chairman and president.
Novak, former chief operating officer for PepsiCola North America, will be responsible for operating the business and developing the Pizza Hut, KFC and Taco Bell brands, PepsiCo said.
Purchase, N.Y.-based PepsiCo's stock was unchanged at $37.125 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning.
